newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares steady in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares steady in moderate trade.

text.p: Norwegian shares recovered from a weak start and clung in positive territory on Thursday despite jittery overseas markets, and some dealers said they saw some consolidation ahead.
Shipping stocks performed strongly, buoyed by firm tanker rates and healthy business in the oil service sector. Oslo's shipping index advanced 0.79 percent to end the session at 1,019.23 points.
The Total share index ended at 1,166.66 points, 0.01 percent higher, in moderate turnover of 763 million crowns.
"The market was relatively strong until the close even though foreign markets are coming down and interest rates are very slightly higher," said one broker.

"There's been a fresh flow of liquidity to the market, especially due to dividend payments, and don't forget that although Norway has been strong this year, it has been the worst performing market in Scandinavia."

Saga Petroleum was the most traded share in turnover terms after the company presented results broadly in line with expectations. Saga closed 0.50 crowns up at 143 crowns in trade worth 58 million crowns.
